items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: I really feel very good of having had the opportunity of working with fellas like the late Monk Hable, the late Larry Shields, and Jeff Riddick

ctx.x: Oh sure, well I knew Monk. He was the first jazz musician in New Orleans that I ever got to know was Monk. And that was when he was working on Broadway in the Alcohol Factory. Right. Walking around in it all day long.

You know Dick, I really feel very good of having had the opportunity of working with fellas like the late Monk Hable, the late Larry Shields, and Jeff Riddick, and the late Almond Hug. Which Shields? Larry Shields. Harry Shields.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: Harry Shields was the brother of the late Larry Shields. And Larry Shields passed away many years ago in California and was responsible for writing clarinet and marmalade, plus a whole flock of other tunes.

ctx.x: Because Arthur Godfrey had, happened to be in Chicago for a week with his horse, Goldie. He has a horse that does tricks. This horse, his name is Goldie. And he happened to be in Chicago that week, staying at the Edgewater Beach Hotel. Because during the day, he was performing at a stock show. His horse was performing at a stock show. And he got, and Arthur Godfrey doesn't go anywhere without his banjo. And he has a beautiful, expensive banjo. And he flipped over the banjo. We were doing two shows a night in…
You know, Arthur Godfrey had some pretty good musicians with him at the time.
